intro: Albanians speak a unique language and are known for religious tolerance and hospitality.

chapters.title: Language and faith
text: Albanian forms its own branch of the Indo-European family, unrelated closely to any other language. Muslims, Orthodox Christians and Catholics live side by side, and marriages between faiths are common.
Tirana is the capital. About as many Albanians live abroad, in Italy, Greece and beyond, as in Albania, and many more live in neighbouring Kosovo.

chapters.title: Customs
text: In traditional Albanian gestures, nodding can mean 'no' and shaking the head 'yes'. Guests are treated with great honour.

keyTerms.meaning: A group of languages within a family that descend from a common ancestor.
